note: depth pass 2: L4 例词补充

words.glossEn: the branch of medicine dealing with the heart
words.etymology: 希腊 kardia「心」+ -logia「学问」
derivation: card（心）+ i + o（连接元音）+ logy（学科）→ 研究心的学问
words.example: He was referred to cardiology for further tests.

words.glossEn: a record of the heart's electrical activity
words.etymology: cardio-「心」+ -gram「记录下来的东西」
derivation: card（心）+ i + o + gram（记录）→ 心的记录图
words.example: The cardiogram showed an irregular rhythm.

words.glossEn: a loud and confused noise of many voices
words.etymology: 拉丁 clamor < clamare「呼喊」
derivation: clam（呼喊）+ -or（名词后缀）→ 呼喊声
words.example: The clamor for reform grew louder each week.

words.glossEn: an official public announcement
words.etymology: 拉丁 proclamatio < pro-（向前）+ clamare（呼喊）
derivation: pro（向前）+ clam（呼喊）+ -ation → 向公众喊出的话
words.example: The governor issued a proclamation on the holiday.

words.glossEn: a ruler with absolute power
words.etymology: 希腊 autokratēs < autos「自己」+ kratos「统治」
derivation: auto（自己）+ crat（统治）→ 独自统治的人
words.example: The founder ran the company like an autocrat.

words.glossEn: government by one person with unlimited power
words.etymology: 希腊 autokrateia < autos「自己」+ kratein「统治」
derivation: auto（自己）+ crac（统治）+ -y → 一人统治
words.example: The country drifted from autocracy to chaos.

words.glossEn: deserving blame
words.etymology: 拉丁 culpabilis < culpa「过错」
derivation: culp（过错）+ -able（可…的）→ 可归咎的
words.example: The report found the manager culpable for the delay.

words.glossEn: the state of being to blame
words.etymology: 晚期拉丁 culpabilitas < culpa「过错」
derivation: culp（过错）+ -abil- + -ity → 应受责备的性质
words.example: The court weighed the culpability of each defendant.

words.glossEn: condemnation to eternal punishment
words.etymology: 拉丁 damnatio < damnare「判定有罪、判罚」
derivation: damn（判罪、损害）+ -ation → 被判罚
words.example: The preacher thundered about damnation and mercy.

words.glossEn: to express strong disapproval of; to sentence
words.etymology: 拉丁 condemnare < con-（加强）+ damnare（判罚）
derivation: con（共同、加强）+ demn（判罚）→ 判定有罪
words.example: World leaders condemned the attack on the hospital.

words.glossEn: to devote something to a purpose or person
words.etymology: 拉丁 dedicare < de-（郑重）+ dicare（宣告）
derivation: de（郑重）+ dic（说、宣告）+ -ate → 郑重宣告归于某人
words.example: She dedicated ten years to the study of beetles.

words.glossEn: to base something on a stated fact; to assert
words.etymology: 拉丁 praedicare < prae-（在前）+ dicare（宣告）
derivation: pre（在前）+ dic（说）+ -ate → 当众说出 → 断言
words.example: The argument is predicated on a false assumption.

words.glossEn: the capacity to do work; vigour
words.etymology: 希腊 energeia < en-（在内）+ ergon（工作）
derivation: en（在内）+ erg（工作）+ -y → 内在的做功能力
words.example: The panel converts sunlight into electrical energy.

words.glossEn: combined action producing more than the parts alone
words.etymology: 希腊 synergia < syn-（共同）+ ergon（工作）
derivation: syn（共同）+ erg（工作）+ -y → 共同做功
words.example: The merger promised synergy between the two labs.

words.glossEn: a speech of high praise, especially for the dead
words.etymology: 希腊 eulogia < eu-（好）+ logos（言辞）
derivation: eu（好）+ logy（言辞）→ 说好话 → 颂词
words.example: His eulogy for the old coach moved the whole hall.

words.glossEn: a feeling of intense happiness
words.etymology: 希腊 euphoria < eu-（好）+ pherein（承受）→ 身体舒泰
derivation: eu（好）+ phor（承受）+ -ia（状态）→ 感觉良好
words.example: The victory brought a brief euphoria to the whole town.

words.glossEn: a person who has escaped and is in hiding
words.etymology: 拉丁 fugitivus < fugere「逃走」
derivation: fug（逃）+ -it- + -ive → 逃跑的人
words.example: The fugitive was caught at a border crossing.

words.glossEn: a place or state of shelter from danger
words.etymology: 拉丁 refugium < re-（回）+ fugere（逃）
derivation: re（回）+ fug（逃）+ -e → 逃回去的地方
words.example: The climbers took refuge in a stone hut.

words.glossEn: to mix up in the mind; to make unclear
words.etymology: 拉丁 confundere < con-（一起）+ fundere（倒、流）
derivation: con（一起）+ fus（倾倒）+ -e → 倒在一起 → 混淆
words.example: The two labels are easy to confuse.

words.glossEn: the process of joining two things into one
words.etymology: 拉丁 fusio < fundere「倾倒、熔化」
derivation: fus（熔化、倾倒）+ -ion → 熔合
words.example: The reactor aims at controlled nuclear fusion.
